newsitem.title: USA: US frozen belly stocks likely dipped in July - trade.
newsitem.headline: US frozen belly stocks likely dipped in July - trade.

text.p: Frozen pork belly stocks in U.S. warehouses declined seasonally during July, but the amount of drop was in question, livestock analysts said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its monthly Cold Storage Report at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT Friday and it is expected to show August 1 pork belly stocks between 26.5 million and 37.0 million lbs, a decrease of 15.3 million to 25.8 million from July 1 stocks of 52.318 million. Stocks on August 1, 1996 were 28.533 million.
Dan Vought, analyst for A.G. Edwards, put stocks at the high end of the estimated range at 37 million lbs, but said it was still a good movement out of warehouses.
"It's still showing pretty good belly demand," Vaught said.

Vaught noted that stocks fell sharply last year in warehouses that do not report to the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, and this may well be the case again this year. Non-reporting stocks went from 15.255 million lbs down to 2.268 million during July 1996, he said.
Other analysts also expect non-reporting warehouses to show the biggest decline in stocks during July and some expect stocks to have fallen under year-earlier levels and to historically low levels.

Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp, estimated stocks at 28.3 million lbs, a decline of 24 million lbs in July. This compared with a decline of 28.2 million last year and a 10-year average of 25.2 million.
This "puts stocks historically low", down to the smallest level since 1976 when frozen stocks were at 26.541 million lbs, he said.
